source: Primary PET/SPECT papers and FDA/EMA review searched 2026-10-03, with escitalopram/lurasidone/milnacipran sourced 2026-10-11. Only values printed as dose/plasma/occupancy observations are marked measured; model thresholds and ED50/figure-only concentrations are retained with explicit qualifiers (statistic + plasma_relation).

pairs.quote: A target occupancy of 80% occurs at a concentration of 3.2 ng/mL

drugs.notes: This is a regulatory-review exposure/occupancy model point, not a raw subject pair; it is retained and labelled accordingly.

pairs.dose_note: single oral dose of S-citalopram, not steady-state daily
pairs.occupancy_note: anterior cingulate = 65%; regional means 59-69% (A cingulate 65, Frontal cortex 67, Temporal cortex 63, Insula 59, Hippocampus 59, Putamen 64, Raphe nuclei 69)

citation.location: Lundberg et al. 2007, Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 10(6):777-785; Table 1 (p.780) and Table 2 (p.782); open access

pairs.quote: Table 1 title: 'Serum drug concentrations after single oral dose of 20 mg R,S-Cit or 10 mg S-Cit (mean+/-S.D., nmol/l)'. S-Cit column row at nominal time 6 h: '6 8 21.6+/-3.6' (time h, n, S-Cit nmol/l). Linking text (p.780): 'The calculated 5-HTT occupancy was related to the mean serum concentration of S-Cit at 6-8 h post-dose, i.e. during the PET measurement.' Table 2 S-Cit 'Mean' row: A cingulate 65, Frontal cortex 67, Temporal cortex 63, Insula 59, Hippocampus 59, Putamen 64, Raphe nuclei 69.

drugs.notes: Serum mean of 8 healthy male subjects at 6 h post single oral dose during the PET scan, paired with the regional mean 5-HTT occupancy. Primary lead Kim 2017 (PMID 27557550) and Baldinger 2014 (PMID 24121201) were paywalled and printed only model EC50s; Lundberg 2007 is the open-access source actually used. Adjacent S-Cit serum time points (same Table 1): 6.5 h 20.4+/-4.5, 7 h 20.3+/-5.0, 7.5 h 20.1+/-4.1, 8 h 20.2+/-4.5 nmol/L.

pairs.dose_note: patients on 80, 120, or 160 mg/day at steady state

citation.location: Potkin et al. 2014, CNS Spectrums (DOI 10.1017/S1092852913000357); abstract; [18F]fallypride

pairs.quote: Blood concentrations greater than 70 ng/mL may be required to achieve a 65% occupancy level in subcortical areas. Blood lurasidone concentration (plus major metabolite), but not dose, significantly correlated with D2 receptor occupancy.

drugs.notes: Modeled requirement across a dose range, not a single measured subject point; the inequality is preserved as plasma_relation '>'. Concentration is lurasidone plus major metabolite. The gold-standard per-subject table (Wong 2013, PMID 23649882) is paywalled and was not quoted; a snippet 'EC50 = 7.6 ng/mL' was rejected as unverifiable.

citation.location: Nogami et al. 2013, Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 16(5):937-943; Results p.940-941 and Fig. 4 legend

pairs.quote: Estimated ED50 was 122.5 mg administration dose and 145.4 ng/ml plasma concentration in 5-HTT and 149.9 mg administration dose and 158.7 ng/ml plasma concentration in NET.

drugs.notes: ED50 values are the hyperbolic-fit parameters (model-fit 50% point), not a single measured subject reading; the paper does not tabulate per-subject plasma/occupancy. Measured-but-unpaired dose/occupancy (thalamus): 5-HTT 33.0% at 50 mg, 38.6% at 100 mg, 60.0% at 150 mg, 61.5% at 200 mg; NET 25.3% at 25 mg, 40.0% at 100 mg, 47.3% at 125 mg, 49.9% at 200 mg.
